answer: Autonomous agents obtain Sybil resistance when identity is bound to a costly, revocable stake and a cryptographic cipher seals a continuous plume of attested work. Each false identity must earn nectar from verifiable contribution, while any forged branch triggers slashing proportional to stake. The net expected utility of Sybil creation becomes negative because marginal cost exceeds bounded rewards, forcing the equilibrium toward unique, economically backed identities.
